unit: a rotation is one verified answer to one isotope; a penny is one rotation
method: one `npm run build` per seed on this machine (node 24.21.0), wall clock. `checks` counts distinct fail() names in the publish guard, `sites` the fail() call lines, `pairs` the declared contrast pairs, `doom`/`a11y` the rule counts, `shells` the pages the overflow gate verifies (one rotation each). `rotations` = sites + pairs + doom + a11y + shells: the floor a cycle can verify, not what a clean run reports.
notes: The two starters are the most expensive cycles (176 and 127 rotations) and the bare children the cheapest (40-45). Cost follows the number of claims a cycle can verify, not the machine.
Wall time is flat: 3.1-5.8 seconds across a fourfold spread in rotations. A gate is paid for in rotations, not seconds.
The accounting itself is nearly free: the rules catch-up is one fetch, the rotation gate reads a committed file. The gates are what cost.
The overflow gate has no waiver list on any seed: a design may be a marquee (zaphood), but a horizontal scrollbar is content the reader cannot reach.
Every seed publishes its own state at /rotations.json (rung, distance, head, rotations per isotope), so an updater reads the record instead of guessing.

tokenCost.extrapolation: The agent pays to change the gates; the machine pays to run them. A five-seed accounting pass cost $0.18 and 296,815 tokens, one-off. A cycle then costs $0 and 3-6 seconds. Extrapolated at $0.013 a gate-installation: doom + a11y + contrast for the two bare children (6 installations, plus justified waivers) is about $0.08-0.12 once, and raises their cycle floor from 40/45 to ~90 at no per-cycle cost.
